$comment: What a tier MEANS, in one place.
Three surfaces decide things from a tier and they had three ideas about it:
jarvis-core gates tier 3 and the gated domains, the console draws an
approval banner, the phone's policy engine raises a device tier — and the
MCP config comment promised '2 = confirm first' while the code ran tier 2
unprompted. A user reading that comment and installing an MCP server got

1.name: direct
1.means: Runs immediately. Reversible, cheap, and visible if it was wrong.

2.name: background
2.means: Runs immediately, and is worth telling the user about — it takes time, costs something, or reaches outside the house. NOT an approval: a tier that asks is tier 3.

3.name: approval
3.means: Held until a human says yes, to that exact call, with the arguments pinned at the moment it was requested. A denial or an expiry runs nothing.

rules.a_server_may_only_raise: A tier arriving from outside (a server telling a device what a call is worth) may RAISE the local tier, never lower it. Pinned by android-app/tools/policy_truth_table_test.py and jarvis-desktop/tests/test_policy.py.
rules.gated_domains: Some domains are tier 3 whatever the tool says, because the domain is the risk: `lock`, `notify`. See jarvis/const.py GATED_DOMAINS.
rules.gated_services: Every tier-3 tool has a service twin in GATED_SERVICES, so an automation cannot call at tier 1 what a model must ask for.
rules.untrusted_raises: After an untrusted result (a web page, screen text, a file), the rest of the turn is raised: a tier-1 call becomes an ask. Content that arrived from outside must not be able to spend the trust of the turn it arrived in.

default_for_mcp.$comment: An MCP server's tools are tier 2 by default: they run, and they are announced. This is written down here because the config comment used to say '2 = confirm first', which the code has never done — and a promise of a confirmation that never comes is worse than no promise.
